notes: This source/test traceability contract covers only Umbra's bounded Unconditional Attribute Ownership Divestiture path in the opt-in, non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile. A successful call validates the whole supplied owner set, immediately makes every supplied attribute unowned, preserves already-pending regular and If Available acquisition paths, and schedules regular follow-up acquisition work before the new ownership-assumption offers. At planning time it groups each currently eligible non-pending joined federate's offered attributes into at most one standard Request Attribute Ownership Assumption callback, carrying the unconditional-divestiture tag. Callback entry rechecks that the recipient still knows the instance, publishes each offered attribute at its known class, remains outside the private regular/If Available/cancellation boundary, and sees the attribute unowned; stale or partial offers are suppressed. The standalone case also records the §7.2 rules for immediate unownership, optional discovery of additional willing federates, and use of Request Attribute Ownership Assumption for eligible non-pending recipients. A selected filesystem report file records the accepted §7.2 invocation before the later callback and retains the service's object-instance, attribute-set, and base-64 user-tag arguments. Table 5's type-63 tag literal conflicts with the companion standard MIM's type-60 UserSuppliedTag value; Umbra keeps the literal isolated to source-backed file text pending an authoritative resolution (RL-077). An offer never transfers ownership itself: the candidate must invoke a standard acquisition service. This bounded slice does not run a continuing search for later joins, discoveries, publications, or other newly eligible federates after the successful divestiture call; it does not claim the complete §7.2 unowned-owner-search lifecycle. Negotiated divestiture, Request Divestiture Confirmation, Confirm Divestiture, negotiated-divestiture cancellation, RTI-owned state, full resign-action ownership disposition, save/restore behavior, DDM, timestamped/retraction behavior, FOM sharing policy, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside the slice. The contract uses immutable candidate IDs and exported clause IDs from the Requirements Lab. RL-015 records the applicable ownership candidate attribution limitations, while RL-076 records the missing structured Table 5 continuation rows.
